decisions.reason: The GPIO assignments remain applicable, but the single-board decision necessarily moves their scope from the obsolete modular main board to the integrated board.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Yes, I think they can, now that there is only one board + sensors/buttons/leds which are all easy to position I think there is no issue wherever you put them

decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already moves the pull-ups and I2C scope to the integrated board and removes the obsolete interboard-cable attribute.
The existing same-message MODIFY already transfers the BOOT and reset circuit scope from the modular main board to the integrated board without changing its electrical behavior.
The source does not alter the panel-input GPIO assignments or connector-based mounting; general connector placement flexibility is owned by the mechanical-layout Requirement.
The existing same-message MODIFY fully captures removal of the modular interboard interface, deletes its obsolete connector and topology attributes, and retains the operational removal fact.
The existing same-message MODIFY already removes the obsolete condition referring to operation without a separate power board and moves the Requirement to the integrated-board context.

The existing same-message MODIFY already updates the measurement coverage and scope for the integrated board; the source does not resolve the separate question of whether an INA monitor can be omitted.
The existing same-message MODIFY directly and completely records the permitted connector placement across the proposed board sides.

The existing same-message MODIFY already converts the former sensor-board role to integrated-board external sensor connections and removes obsolete main-board input connectors and the old total connector count.
The Requirement was already scoped to the integrated board, and the source does not change the AXP2101 battery, USB, charging, or rail behavior.
The existing same-message MODIFY already transfers native USB programming from the modular main-board context to the integrated board without changing the USB-C interface.
The existing same-message MODIFY already places the power-button connector and PWRON connection on the integrated board and records its flexible connector placement.
